source_locator.edition_or_translation: J. M. Ashmand translation from Proclus's Greek paraphrase; 1900 W. Foulsham & Co. new edition
source_locator.section: Faces, Chariots, and Other Similar Attributes of the Planets
source_locator.short_quote: Venus is in her proper face when making a sextile aspect to either luminary, provided she be occidental to the Sun, but oriental to the Moon

prerequisites: Venus aspect to the Sun or Moon
printed Sun-relative and Moon-relative orientation conditions
calculation_dependencies: Venus angular separation from a luminary
source-defined orientation relative to the Sun and Moon
normalized_rule: In Ashmand's wording, Venus's proper-face example involves a sextile aspect to the Sun or Moon with the printed orientation qualifications; whether those qualifications are simultaneous or correspond to alternative luminary targets remains unresolved.
synthesis_notes: This is a traditional relational classification, not a claim about later decan dignity or scientifically measured facial appearance.
review_notes: Keep the candidate unresolved. The Ashmand syntax does not establish whether the two printed orientation conditions are simultaneous or correspond to alternative luminary targets; do not implement either reading as settled.
transmission_notes: The cited sentence is syntactically ambiguous in the Ashmand/Proclus transmission: 'to either luminary' may be read with simultaneous qualifications or with target-corresponding alternatives. The later decan/face technique is not automatically equivalent to this Ptolemaic proper-face example.
